newsitem.title: GREECE: Position squaring feeds Greek short rate firmness.
newsitem.headline: Position squaring feeds Greek short rate firmness.

text.p: Players continued to close out positions driving Greek short-term money rates higher 15 basis points compared to morning levels in late active trading, traders said.

"Short-term money rates are up 15 basis points in late active dealing as some banks seek to square positions," said a money market dealer at a foreign bank. "Part of the hike relates to Thursday's ECU purchases at the fixing."
Other traders said they expected the market to get nervous as national elections on September 22 neared and drachma liquidity was more or less balanced.

Some dealers did not rule out limited speculative moves to test the waters but others disagreed saying there was no indication of such a development from three-month money, the speculative tool in the past.
The central bank drained overnight money at an unchanged 12.40 percent.
Early elections will be held September 22 but the market has taken a positive attitude towards them on the grounds that the winner will have no option but to follow Greece's EU convergence plan.
The mark was quoted at 159.65/75 drachmas from Friday's 159.660 fix, the dollar at 237.22/32 drachmas from 237.040 and the Ecu at 301.19/29 from 301.270 drachmas.
"Fixing was neutral in terms of the inflows, outflows balance," said a trader. "A foreign player sold 50 million ECUs for drachmas after the fixing."
